newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU grain export commitments exceed 26 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: EU grain export commitments exceed 26 mln tonnes.

text.p: European Union grain export commitments up to April 22 are up 66 percent over last year, official figures showed on Friday.

Figures supplied by member country officials showed grain earmarked for export between July 1, 1996 and April 22, 1997 totalled 26.558 million tonnes against 15.956 million during the same period last year.
Exports of commercial soft wheat grain reached 9.786 million tonnes against 5.62 million a year ago.
Soft wheat flour exports jumped to 5.766 million tonnes from 3.675 million.
Barley exports reached 6.069 million tonnes against 1.318 million tonnes and malt exports 2.669 milion tonnes against 2.198 million tonnes.
On Thursday the European Union rejected all bids to export free market and intervention grain at its weekly auction.
Last week it had closed the weekly tender for soft wheat exports but had kept open a daily bidding channel.
But on Thursday the EU decided that a tax of 15 Ecus per tonne would apply to daily soft wheat grain exports as soon as the relevant EU regulation is published in the official journal.

The EU also decided a tax of 20 Ecus per tonne would apply to daily soft wheat flour exports. The tax for durum wheat grain exports was set at 10 Ecus and that for durum semolina at 15 Ecus. A zero refund still applies to daily barley exports while malting barley exports now carry a nil value refund.
Weekly tenders to export barley, rye, oats and durum wheat and Greek maize from the open market are still open and similar tenders to export intervention rye and barley also stay open.
The Commission will be shut for public holidays on May 1 and May 8, so the next weekly grain auction will be held on May 15. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
